steps: Fireplace size & hearth
Confirm the masonry fireplace meets the minimum opening in Figure 2 and its non-combustible hearth extends 16" in front of and 8" beyond each side of the opening.

The minimum fireplace dimensions are given only as a drawing (Figure 2); check the opening against that page.

The non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the existing fireplace opening.

Ember protection over combustible flooring (p. 13): USA 16" to the firing side (from the glass) and 8" to each side of the door opening; Canada 18" to the firing side and 8" to each side of the unit.
Clearances to combustibles
From the blower covers: 10" to an adjacent sidewall, 6" to side facing (max 3-1/2" deep). From the top of the cast top: 12" to a mantel or mantel facing; maximum mantel depth 12".
Prepare the fireplace & chimney
Masonry wood-burning fireplace only, chimney at least 15' from the hearth, no shared flue. Sweep and inspect, finish repairs, then lock the damper open or remove it.

• Fireplace built to NFPA 211 or applicable codes; installation to CAN/CSA-B365. Never in a factory-built fireplace, and never a makeshift or "temporary" install.
  • Don't connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance. Mobile homes: not in a sleeping room.
  • Have the chimney swept and inspected. Check for creosote, obstructions, cracks, loose mortar or other defects; complete repairs before installing.
  • Lock the damper open or remove it completely. Don't remove bricks or mortar, except masonry or steel (including the damper plate) from the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame where needed for a liner, provided the structure isn't weakened and required protection for combustibles isn't reduced.
  • If the fireplace has been modified for the insert, fasten the supplied metal tag to its back wall.
  • The insert is heavy: install with two people, with cardboard or a heavy blanket on the hearth.
Install the liner & flue collar
Feed the stainless liner down and fit a stove-to-liner adapter. Unbolt the 6" collar (two bolts), fix it to the adapter with three stainless screws and caulk with high-temp stove cement.

Full flue liner (required in Canada)

Continuous liner from the flue collar to the top of the chimney, class 3 per CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640. Measure from the top of the existing chimney flue to the hearth floor, allowing extra for flashing and rain cap. Feed the liner from the top, through the damper area into the fireplace cavity, and attach the adapter per the liner maker's instructions.

Direct flue connection (USA only)

Full or partial stainless rigid or flex liner, type HT (2100°F) per UL1777. Measure from the top of the first chimney flue tile to the top of the insert, allowing extra to go into the tile; feed the liner through the damper area into the first flue tile and seal where it passes through the chimney throat. A clean-out door may be required by local code. Then follow the same collar, leveling and flashing steps. Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner as the safest installation with optimum performance.

Collar

Remove the collar (two bolts), attach it to the adapter with three stainless screws, caulk around the connections with high-temp stove cement and check the gasket is in good shape.
Strip, set & level
Remove both blower covers (Torx screw, top rear corner), the cast top (two wing bolts) and the baffle. Push the insert into the fireplace and level it with the front or rear leveling legs.

Moving the fan speed control to the left side? Do it before fitting the surround and installing in the fireplace (p. 21).

Leveling legs (bolts) are supplied for an uneven hearth (p. 13):

  • Fireplace lower than the hearth: fit the rear bolts in the threaded inserts under the sides toward the rear, set to the depth of the drop.
  • Hearth lower than the fireplace floor: fit the front bolts in the threaded inserts under the front, toward the sides.

Push the insert into position and adjust the bolts to level it.
Secure the collar, flash & cap

Reach through the flue opening and pull the collar down with the supplied tool until the bolts pass through; fit the clamps and nuts, centre the collar and tighten. Flash the chimney top and fit a rain cap.

1. Pull the collar down with the tool provided until its bolts pass through the flue opening; install the clamps and nuts, centre the collar on the opening and tighten.
  2. Measure, trim and shape a chimney-top flashing to the existing flue with a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side; set it over the liner, seated firmly against the flue tile.
  3. Attach a rain cap to the liner. A storm collar may be used if desired.
Combustion air

Outside air: swap the ash clean-out cover for a rodent screen, keep the air inlet clear and seal the surround. Room air: take off the Decorative Cover under the ash lip, remove and discard the Room Air Cover, then refit the Decorative Cover.
Electrical

Plug the blowers into a properly grounded three-prong outlet; never route the cord under the unit or against hot or sharp surfaces. The manual rates the blowers at 120V on p. 19 and 115V on the label.

Electrical Supply (p. 19)120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A
Rating label (p. 3)115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP
Note: the manual gives the blowers' electrical rating as 120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A in the Electrical Supply section on p. 19 and as 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP on the rating label on p. 3.

Don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Follow local codes, or the CSA C22.2 Canadian Electrical Code / NEC ANSI/NFPA 70. Wiring is shown in Figure 8.
Surround, top & fan covers

Bolt surround panels A, B and C together (1/4" x 1/2" bolts), slide it over the unit behind the ash shelf into the bracket slots and push back to the fireplace face. Refit the cast top (wing bolts) and fan covers.

1. Remove the fan covers and the decorative top (two wing bolts underneath; pull it toward you out of its brackets).
  2. Lay surround parts A, B and C face down on a flat, non-marring surface and bolt them together at points "D" with the 1/4" x 1/2" bolts and nuts.
  3. Stand it upright; check the face is flat and even at the joints and sides.
  4. Slide it over the unit behind the ash shelf and engage the tabs on its back into the surround bracket slots.
  5. Push the whole appliance back until the surround contacts the fireplace face.
  6. Refit the decorative top (wing bolts in the slots, pushed gently back against the surround) and tighten. Fit the fan covers; their outer tabs use the surround's slots.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Build every fire directly on the firebricks. Never use a grate or andirons to raise the wood.

  1. Move the air control to High (all the way to the left) and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the firebox and crisscross several pieces of dry kindling over it. Add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" to 1" until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame.
  4. Add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. Once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, set the air control for normal burning.
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any other chemical or volatile liquid to start or "freshen up" a fire. Keep all such liquids well away from the insert while it is in use. Fire starters made of paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine.

Your first 2-3 fires

The paint bakes on during the first few fires and gives off smoke and fumes. Open all windows and doors, and follow the Stove Bright paint sheet that came with your insert. Smoke detectors may go off more often while it cures. Don't disconnect them.

Keep the door closed while it burns; this insert isn't designed for open-door burning. The glass and outer surfaces get hot enough to burn, so keep children, clothing and furniture away.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The air control sets how hard the fire burns.

High "H"all the way to the left. Use it only for lighting and for preheating fresh loads.
Low "L"pushed to the far right

Finding your setting

Every home's heating needs differ, so the right setting comes from trial and error. Note what works for future fires. It also shifts with the type of wood, outside temperature, chimney size and weather.

If smoke pours down across the glass (a "waterfall"), you've turned the air down too soon or too low.

The lowest burn rate is set at the factory. Altering it is against federal regulations, and tampering with the air control voids the warranty.

Draft warning signs

  • Too much draft: an uncontrollable burn, or a stove part or chimney glowing red.
  • Too little draft: smoke puffing back into the room, or leaking into the room at the insert and pipe joints.
Don't over-fire. A glowing red top or vent pipe means the fire is too hot. It can permanently damage the insert and chimney, and may void the warranty.

reload.title: Reloading & overnight burns
reload.html:
To add wood

  1. Move the air control to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly. This keeps smoke from puffing back into the room.
  3. Load dry wood endwise, up to 18" long, so air can flow between the logs.
  4. Don't load so high that opening the door becomes hazardous, and make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass.

For the cleanest burn, add small loads (two or three logs, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load) and leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes. After about 30 minutes you can turn it down a lot.

Overnight burns

Use unsplit logs. Char the load completely on the maximum setting before turning the air down. Never try to burn overnight with green or wet wood.

Restarting in the morning

  1. Open the door, rake the hot embers toward the front and add a couple of dry, split logs. Close the door.
  2. Set the air to High. The logs should catch within a few minutes.
  3. Once the wood has charred, reset the air to your usual setting.
Fire won't last the night? The manual's chart lists: air set too high, not enough wood (unsplit is best), too much draft, or a leaking door gasket.

wood.title: Choosing and testing your wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwoods give higher efficiency and lower emissions than softwoods or green wood.

  • Season (air-dry) wood for six months or more.
  • Store it under cover, away from open flame or heat sources.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good, large bed of coals:

Dryburning on more than one side within one minute
Dampturns black and lights within three minutes
Soakedsizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes. Don't burn it.

Never burn

Wet or green wood, unseasoned wood, garbage, treated wood, salt-water wood, coal or charcoal, plastics, rubber or tires, lawn clippings or yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, anything containing asbestos, construction or demolition debris, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners, solvents or asphalt products, or paper products, cardboard, plywood and particleboard. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes or make the insert ineffective and cause smoke. Charcoal can produce deadly carbon monoxide. Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that rapidly destroy metal and void the warranty. Never barbecue in the insert.

Note: on wet wood, the manual's do-not-burn list (p. 6) includes wet or green wood and unseasoned wood, and p. 5 says not to burn wet wood; but p. 7 says that if you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air control set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures, and not to attempt to burn overnight using green wood or wet wood.
Newspaper and fire starters made of paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass with fireplace glass cleaner, and only when the insert is cold.

  • Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape with anything that could scratch the glass.
  • Don't slam the door or knock the glass. Before closing the door, check that no logs stick out.
  • If the glass cracks or breaks, replace it before using the insert again. Use only the ceramic replacement glass from your dealer.

What the film tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion, dry wood and fairly clean pipes. A black, greasy film that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly, and it's building up at least as fast in the chimney.

Glass keeps getting dirty? The manual lists wet wood, turning the air down before there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, low draft, or a leaking door gasket as causes.

A plated door: clean it with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.

ash.title: Removing the ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out only when the insert is cold, after the fire has burned down and cooled.

  • Remove the excess whenever ash gets 3" to 4" deep in the firebox.
  • Leave an ash bed about 1" deep on the firebox bottom. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  • Keep the front of the firebox clear. That's where the boost air for the fire comes in, and built-up ash blocks it.

Safe disposal

  • Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  • Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn.
  • If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all cinders have thoroughly cooled.
  • Don't put other waste in the ash container.

blower.title: The blower fans
blower.html:
Your insert has twin variable-speed circulating air blowers. A rocker switch chooses automatic or manual, and the fan speed control sets the speed. The speed control is under the ash lip on the right-hand side, unless your installer moved it to the left.

Rocker switch at OffAutomatic: the blowers start once the insert is up to temperature, and stop after the fire is out and it has cooled
Rocker switch at OnManual: bypasses the temperature switch for full control

Suggested settings

  • Air control at "L" (pushed to the far right): run the blowers on Low.
  • Air control anywhere above "L": any blower speed you like.
Clean the blowers at least every six months: remove the covers and vacuum the blower openings to clear dust and debris.
Unplug first. Disconnect the power before servicing; there's a risk of electrical shock.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave creosote on the chimney lining. If it ignites, it makes an extremely hot fire; temperatures inside the chimney can exceed 2000°F.

Keep it clean

  • Have the chimney and connector inspected at least once every two months during the heating season. Remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Pacific Energy recommends inspecting the liner and connector monthly and having the liner cleaned every year, or more often if needed.
  • Until experience shows how often you need to clean, check for creosote daily.
  • Burn dry wood with plenty of air, and don't turn the air down too soon after loading.
  • Avoid very hot fires: trash, cardboard, Christmas tree limbs, or a full load on hot coals with the air wide open longer than it takes to char.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting from the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or a vibrating chimney.

If it happens: get everyone ready to leave and meet at your agreed spot outside. Close the air control and call the fire department, with an extinguisher handy. Before the next fire, have the chimney cleaned and checked for cracks, and check the combustibles around the chimney and roof.

maint.title: Maintenance checks
maint.html:
Look for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracking) · door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBaffle and its locking pin · brick rails and tabs · air riser tube · back of the airwash chamber · boost tube cover · liner and connector
Every six monthsVacuum out the blowers (at minimum)
Every yearHave the liner cleaned (more often if needed)

Door gasket

The 7/8" fiberglass rope gasket needs only light pressure to seal. Keep it in good condition; if it needs replacing, use kit 80000156 from your Pacific Energy dealer.

Baffle and firebrick

Some warping of the baffle at the top of the firebox, up to 1/4", is normal. Call your dealer if it's warped more, cracked or broken. Never burn with the baffle or its insulation removed. Replace broken or missing firebricks.

Running with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty. Use only materials supplied by the manufacturer.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's limited lifetime warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (parts only)Porcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage, not impact), plating, firebox, baffle
3 year comprehensiveParts and labor on any defective part for three years from the date of purchase, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches
Note: on how long this coverage lasts, the manual calls it limited lifetime but adds "(10 years)" in the same heading on p. 30.

Not covered

  • Labor under the lifetime coverage, and firebox rails and heat shields.
  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets.
  • Parts showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Premature wear is a significant sign of improper use, such as excessive draft, heating too large an area or contaminated fuel. These conditions may void the warranty.

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, and the model name and serial number. Register your insert at pacificenergy.net/register.

specRating.title: EPA rating & efficiency
specRating.html:
EPA certified emissions1.8 g/hr
HHV tested efficiency71%
Maker's website: Efficiency (HHV) 71.3%.
LHV tested efficiency77%
EPA BTU output12,518 to 38,177 Btu/hr

Meets the 2020 EPA crib wood emission limits (Method 28R). Efficiencies are weighted averages per CSA B415; the output range uses that efficiency and the burn rates of the low and high EPA tests with Douglas Fir dimensional lumber.

The minimum low burn rate is set at the factory and must not be altered (federal regulations). Rating label: bottom back corner of the side casing, door-catch side.

specFuel.title: Fuel & wood length
specFuel.html:
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Maximum wood length18 inches
Ideal wood length16-18 inches
Maker's website: Log Size (Recommended) 16".

Solid wood fuel only. No grate or andirons: the fire is built directly on the firebricks. Wood air-dried six months or more, loaded endwise.

specFlue.title: Flue, liner & chimney
specFlue.html:
Masonry wood-burning fireplaces only, never a factory-built fireplace, and never on a flue serving another appliance.

Flue collar6" I.D., removable (two bolts)
Chimney height (from hearth)15' (minimum)
CanadaFull liner, collar to chimney top: CAN/ULC-S635 class 3 or CAN/ULC-S640
USAFull liner (recommended) or direct flue connection; liner type HT (2100°F) per UL1777

Direct connection (USA only): liner from the collar into the first chimney flue tile, with a seal in the chimney throat; local code may require a clean-out door. Pacific Energy recommends a full liner for correct draft, avoiding difficult start-ups and smoking out the door.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Minimum clearances when installed in a masonry fireplace (Figure 4):

Side of blower cover to adjacent sidewall10 in. (255 mm)
Side of blower cover to side facing (max 3-1/2 in. deep)6 in. (155 mm)
Top of cast top to mantel facing12 in. (305 mm)
Top of cast top to mantel12 in. (305 mm)
Maximum mantel depth12 in.

The rating label (p. 3) gives the same values (sidewall 10", mantel 12", top facing 12", side facing 6"), headed "measured from fan covers".

specHearth.title: Hearth & ember protection
specHearth.html:
The fireplace's non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front of and 8" beyond each side of the existing fireplace opening (p. 12, where Figure 2 draws the minimum fireplace opening).

Combustible flooring in front of the insert must be protected from hot embers by non-combustible material:

USA16" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the door opening
Canada18" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the unit

Codes: NFPA 211 (USA), CAN/CSA-B365 (Canada). Figure 3 shows the layout. Front or rear leveling bolts are supplied for an uneven hearth.

specAir.title: Combustion air
specAir.html:
Consult local building codes. Combustion air is supplied one of two ways:

Outside air

Remove the cover from the ash clean-out in the existing fireplace and put a rodent screen in its place. Install without covering the air inlet opening. When done, seal the surround to the fireplace and anywhere else air may enter, so combustion air is drawn from outside into the intake on the bottom of the appliance.

Room air

Remove the two screws securing the Decorative Cover under the ash lip, remove the screws holding the Room Air Cover to the base bottom and discard that cover, then refit the Decorative Cover (Figure 7). Air is then drawn from the room through the front of the unit.

Stove won't burn? Check the outside air supply for obstruction and that the room air cover has been removed (p. 25).

specElec.title: Electrical (blowers)
specElec.html:
Electrical Supply (p. 19)120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A
Rating label (p. 3)115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP
Note: the manual gives the blowers' electrical rating as 120V, 60 Hz, 1.2 A in the Electrical Supply section on p. 19 and as 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP on the rating label on p. 3.

Use a properly grounded outlet that accepts a three-pronged plug; don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Never route the cord under the unit; keep it clear of hot or sharp surfaces. Follow local codes, or the CSA C22.2 Canadian Electrical Code / NEC ANSI/NFPA 70. Disconnect power before servicing.

The fan speed controller is factory-installed under the ash lip on the right-hand side and can be moved to the left (pp. 21-22), ideally before fitting the surround and installing in the fireplace. Wiring: Figure 8.

specSurround.title: Surround dimensions
specSurround.html:
Optional surrounds; A and B are the lettered dimensions marked on Figure 1.

Regular surround · A / B43 3/8" / 29 5/8"
Oversized surround · A / B48" / 33 5/8"
Maker's website: Design Options: Embossed Surround, Standard Size (43" x 29"); Embossed Surround, Oversize (48" x 33").

Parts (Met Black): regular 11250043, oversized 11250044. The insert's own dimensions are shown only as a drawing (Figure 1), along with the 6" I.D. flue collar.

review.notes: Single 32-page installation & operation manual; p. 31 is blank apart from the footer, p. 32 is the back cover. The rating label (p. 3) is shared with the Alderlea T5 Insert LE and states 'Certified for use in Canada and U.S.A.' and EPA 2020 compliance; relevant to the catalog's US-availability note. Not transcribed (drawings with unlabeled numbers, linked instead): insert dimensions (Figure 1, p. 11), minimum fireplace opening (Figure 2, p. 12), ember-protection layout (Figure 3, p. 13), clearance layout (Figure 4, p. 14). Surround sizes are given as the p. 11 table's lettered A/B values; which is width or height is only on the figure. Figure 3 labels the Canadian ember protection '18" / 406mm' (406 mm is the US 16" figure); the text and rating label give 18" / 457 mm. The guide uses inches only. The rating label heads its clearances 'measured from fan covers'; p. 14 measures the mantel clearances from the top of the cast top. The guide uses the p. 14 wording. Sequence note: p. 16 step 10 installs the surround after the collar, flashing and cap, while the p. 20 surround procedure ends by pushing the whole appliance back to the fireplace face; the guide keeps the manual's order. Catalog values the manual does not state: max cordwood output, heating area, burn time, firebox volume, weight, glass area, non-catalytic combustion. Catalog EPA output matches the manual's 38,177 Btu/hr within rounding; the website's HHV efficiency (71.3%) differs from the manual's 71% and is noted in specRating. No code table (codes empty). No French-only safety text or scrambled-font text found; French on the label duplicates the English. Firebrick layout (pp. 26-27), ash lip replacement (pp. 23-24) and the parts list (pp. 28-29) are not summarized beyond the part numbers used in drawers.
